findings.title: CSRF/replay: state reused from pipeline.signature without binding to session nonce
findings.body: The state check compares `request.GET.get('state')` directly to `pipeline.signature`, which is a deterministic value derived from pipeline state rather than a per-session random nonce. If an attacker can predict or capture this signature (e.g., via logs, referrer leakage, or by initiating their own pipeline with similar session state), they could craft a matching callback to replay or cross-link an OAuth flow. Typically CSRF-state tokens should be freshly generated random values stored server-side and compared, not a reproducible signature of pipeline data.

findings.title: No validation of error/exception responses from token exchange and user info calls
findings.body: `safe_urlopen`/`safe_urlread` and `get_user_info` calls are wrapped only loosely: body parsing failures fall back to an empty dict silently (bare except swallowing all exceptions), and `get_user_info` is called without any try/except — if GitHub returns a non-200 or malformed response, `get_user_info` could raise an unhandled exception (e.g., ApiError) instead of being caught and converted to a friendly `error()` response, resulting in a raw 500 to the user instead of the intended integration-failed page.

findings.title: KeyError risk if integration.metadata lacks 'sender'
findings.body: `integration.metadata['sender']['login']` is accessed directly without checking existence. If an installation's metadata doesn't contain a 'sender' key (e.g., legacy integrations installed before this feature, or integrations created via other paths), this raises a KeyError instead of gracefully failing with the intended `error()` response, causing an unhandled 500 instead of a user-friendly error page.

findings.title: Hardcoded provider_id check reduces extensibility without clear doc
findings.body: Replacing the list-based `FORWARD_INSTALL_FOR` constant with an inline string literal check (`provider_id == 'github'`) removes the previous extension point for other providers needing the same install-redirect behavior; if another provider needs similar handling in the future, this requires modifying this file directly rather than extending a configurable list, which was arguably better practice given multiple pipeline-based integrations exist.
